facts.raw_span: A white woman in her early 40s presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards
Clinical image showing unspecific erythematous papules on the arm
Clinical image showing scales, crusts, and fissures on the lower lip
Hematoxylin-eosin staining demonstrates spongiosis and erosions over the epidermis and a nodular infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis composed of lymphoid aggregates with ample germinal centers

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and scales, along with the phototest results showing erythema after UV-A irradiation, are consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.

The patient's history of generalized pruritus, lack of response to topical corticosteroids, and physical examination findings of erythematous papules and excoriations are consistent with Atopic Dermatitis.

The patient's skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, are consistent with Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms of erythema and papules after UV-A irradiation, along with the phototest results, are consistent with Polymorphic Light Eruption.
The patient's physical examination findings of erythematous papules, scales, and fissures on the lower lip are consistent with Lichen Planus.
The patient's symptoms of erythema after UV-A irradiation, along with the phototest results, are consistent with Photodermatitis.
The patient's physical examination findings of erythematous papules, scales, and fissures are consistent with Psoriasis.

The patient's skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, are consistent with Dermatomyositis.

rationales.F01: Generalized pruritus is a common symptom in several dermatological conditions.
rationales.F03: Lack of response to topical corticosteroids may indicate a more severe or resistant condition.
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and excoriations are typical skin lesions in various dermatoses.
rationales.F05: Scales and fissures on the lower lip can be seen in lichen planus.
rationales.F07: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a germinal center is highly suggestive of cutaneous lymphoma or chronic actinic dermatitis.
rationales.F09: Delayed erythema after UV-A exposure is characteristic of chronic actinic dermatitis and polymorphic light eruption.
rationales.F12: The biopsy findings of spongiosis, erosions, and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a germinal center are highly indicative of cutaneous lymphoma or chronic actinic dermatitis.
